links.outcome: Errors (inaccuracies, omissions, hallucinations) in LLM-generated discharge summary narratives vs physician-written
links.effect: LLM narratives averaged 2.91 errors per summary vs 1.82 for physicians; LLM narratives were less comprehensive (3.72 vs 4.13, P < .001).
links.quote: LLM-generated narratives contained more unique errors (mean [SD] errors per summary, 2.91 [2.54]) than physician-generated narratives (mean [SD] errors per summary, 1.82 [1.94]).

links.outcome: Potential harmfulness of errors in unreviewed LLM-drafted discharge summaries
links.effect: Narrative-level harm was low but higher for LLM (0.84 vs 0.36, P < .001); 1 LLM narrative scored 4 or greater vs 0 for physicians; 6 vs 5 individual errors scored 4+.
links.quote: Both LLM- and physician-generated narratives had low overall potential for harm (scores <1 on a scale ranging from 0-7), with LLM-generated narratives scoring higher than physician narratives (mean [SD] score of 0.84 [0.98] vs 0.36 [0.70]; P < .001) and only 1 LLM-generated narrative (compared with 0 physician-generated narratives) scoring 4 or greater.

screen.reason: The study evaluated the quality, safety, and error rates of LLM-generated hospital discharge summaries compared with physician-written summaries in a retrospective reader study, but did not test an implementation safeguard or deployment practice.
